definitions.explanation: Juice extracted from fruit. Commonly seen on beverage labels and in food-related contexts.

examples.japanese: この{飲|の}み{物|もの}には{果汁|かじゅう}が{入|はい}っていますか。
examples.english: Does this drink contain fruit juice?

examples.japanese: {搾|しぼ}りたての{果汁|かじゅう}でカクテルを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a cocktail with freshly squeezed fruit juice.

notes:
{果汁|かじゅう} is the formal/technical term for fruit juice, commonly seen on product labels and packaging rather than in casual conversation.

WORD FORMATION:
{果|か} (fruit) + {汁|じゅう} (juice, liquid).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {果汁|かじゅう}100%: 100% fruit juice (common label)
- {果汁|かじゅう}{入|い}り: containing fruit juice
- {搾|しぼ}りたての{果汁|かじゅう}: freshly squeezed juice
- {果汁|かじゅう}{飲料|いんりょう}: fruit juice beverage

USAGE:
In Japan, beverage labels must state the {果汁|かじゅう} percentage. Products with less than 100% are labeled as {果汁|かじゅう}○○% or {果汁|かじゅう}{入|い}り.

CONTRAST:
- {果汁|かじゅう}: fruit juice (formal, label term)
- ジュース: juice (casual everyday word; in Japanese, can also mean any sweet drink, not just fruit juice)
- {果実|かじつ}: fruit (the whole fruit, not the juice)
